stem:
Xavier multiplies $\dfrac{2}{5}\times\dfrac{3}{7}$ and then $\dfrac{3}{7}\times\dfrac{2}{5}$. He asks whether the products differ.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Call both products "fraction factors" only, without comparing the effect of changing factor order.
Say that writing the same product is what creates the two factor orders, instead of the order change leaving the product unchanged.
Report $\dfrac{2}{5}$ as the product only because $\dfrac{2}{5}$ is the first printed fraction in the stem.

teacher.key_rationale: Fraction multiplication is commutative: both orders give $\frac{6}{35}$. Naming only "fraction factors", reversing product and order, or grabbing the first printed fraction all miss that hinge.
